_why:
Eighteen institutional edges around DoD, the House, the congressional oversight mechanism and DoD SAPCO. Each already carried a precise note; each is now given the source that note actually rests on, chosen per edge rather than by rule - the Skidmore aggregation for the Michigan State edge, NORAD's own release for Langley, the DIA reading-room files for the Reid meetings, GAO/NSIAD-95-187 for the 509th, AFPD 16-7 for SAF/AAZ.

One of them needed more than a source. dod-sapco -> sap-annual-report carried the note '[Re-pointed from a collapsed duplicate, 14 Aug 2026.]', which records where the edge came from rather than what it asserts. Rewritten: 10 U.S.C. 119(a)(1) puts the annual SAP report on the Secretary of Defense, and DoDD 5205.07 vests central management of the enterprise in DoD SAPCO under the Deputy Secretary, which is the office it is compiled through. Worth checking whether other collapse placeholders survive elsewhere.

Note hygiene: my first version of the sap-annual-report note quoted the placeholder it replaced, to explain the rewrite. That is the same fault in a different form - an edge note renders in the dock, and a reader should get what the edge asserts, not a narration of its editing history. The explanation belongs here.

edges.note: DoD SAPCO is the office this report is compiled through. 10 U.S.C. 119(a)(1) puts the obligation on the Secretary of Defense - 'not later than March 1 of each year, the Secretary of Defense shall submit to the defense committees a report on special access programs' - and DoDD 5205.07 vests central management of the SAP enterprise in DoD SAPCO under the Deputy Secretary of Defense. The statute names the Secretary; the directive names the office that does the work.
